datingPagesAClassBrings.note: When a class page is published, the pages it links to can take the class's date. Shared because the date is what ORDERS a page on the site, both apps write it, and the Python installer already follows the same convention when it pre-populates a course.

frontmatterKey.why: A page inside the section's own folder belongs to one section and carries 'created'. A course-level page is shared between sections and carries one key per section, so hiding or dating it for section 1 says nothing about section 2.

movesWhen: the page is reached by following links from a class page being published
the page is HIDDEN right now, so this publish is the first time students will see it
the page is not itself a class page
doesNotMoveWhen: the page is already visible to students - it has a place on the site somebody may have linked to or looked at, and republishing a class must not shuffle work that was already out
the page named for publishing is not a class page - there is no class day to inherit
the page is a class page - a class's date is its position in the schedule and nothing may move it
the page is reached only THROUGH another class page - the walk stops at a class, so material a different class brings takes that class's date and not this one's (issue #173, 2026-09-19)

reachStopsAtAClassPage.why: The same rule as shared-rules.json -> followingLinks.stopsAtAClassPage, said here because this is where the date half is specified. A class page never INHERITS a date on either platform and never did; what was decided in #173 is that the walk does not continue PAST it either. It applies wherever a class's date is followed outwards: at publish time, and when a whole section is re-dated from a new timetable - where material behind another class is now claimed by the class that actually brings it rather than by whichever earlier class could see it through that one.

cases.name: a worksheet behind another class keeps its own date
named together, the class that brings it dates it

sharedPagesMoveToo.why: A page several classes link to still moves, as long as students have never seen it. An earlier rule left shared pages alone - 'a concept page linked from three different lessons belongs to none of them' - which is sound for a page already on the site and beside the point for one nobody can reach. A page students cannot see has no place to be left in; it has only the day its FILE was made, which is a fact about the teacher's evening rather than about the course.

whenSeveralClassesShareAPage.why: The same convention the course installer already uses - first_use_dates in setup_course.py dates a shared page to the first class that references it - so a pre-populated course and a hand-published one date their pages the same way. Ties are broken by page title so two classes on one day give the same answer every run rather than depending on folder order.

bothRoutesAgree.why: Naming the class ('publish Unit 2, Day 3') and naming its day ('publish tomorrow's class') are two ways of saying one thing and must date pages identically. They did not: the by-day route worked the dates out and the by-name route passed an empty list, so the same teacher got two different results depending on which sentence they used.

neverPublishedIsInferred.from: the page being hidden at the moment the publish is planned
neverPublishedIsInferred.why: Nothing on disk records a page's history. A page published once and later hidden therefore counts as never published and would take a new date. Recording the truth would mean a new frontmatter key on every page, agreed between both apps and the Python; the inference costs nothing and is right in every case anybody has met.

datingNonClassPages.note: Pages that are not linked from a Unit x, Day y page, and are not themselves a Unit x, Day y page (such as sidebar pages, Curriculum pages, and Key Links pages not referenced in any class lesson), inherit the same date as the first class of the year (Unit 1, Day 1) when a site is previewed or deployed, and upon course setup.
appliesTo: sidebar pages (e.g., folder index.md files — the section landing page carries its newest published class's date)
Key Links pages that are not linked from any Unit x, Day y class page
Curriculum pages (index, expectation notes, and unreferenced expectations)
standalone reference or utility pages not linked from any class page
datingNonClassPages.dateInherited: the date of Unit 1, Day 1 (or the earliest class of the year)
datingNonClassPages.why: Pages that serve the course as a whole belong to the start of the semester rather than carrying arbitrary install timestamps, changing build timestamps, or file creation times.

cases.name: renames run highest day first
cases.why: Working UP would try to make Day 2 into Day 3 while a real Day 3 is still called that: either it overwrites a lesson, or — with a never-overwrite guard — it silently skips, leaving two pages claiming to be Day 3. Working down means every destination has already been vacated.

cases.name: later units move their dates but are not renumbered
cases.why: Unit 2 Day 1 stays Unit 2 Day 1 — its number means something to the teacher. It is the DATE that shifts, because the new class takes a teaching day.

cases.name: a page named some other way is left where it is
cases.why: The trip keeps its date and its name, and the plan SAYS so before the teacher agrees — an unnumbered page silently keeping a date that everything around it moved off is the kind of thing noticed weeks later.

cases.name: a numbered course renames highest first, one number
cases.why: The same order rule as the first case, under the one-number scheme (#267): “make room at Week 2” names ONE number, and no page may be renamed onto a name still in use. A runner builds the position from `insertAtNumber` however its planner holds it.

cases.name: a numbered course keeps its gaps: a later page never moves earlier
cases.why: CODING's own dates: a weekly club whose pages for weeks 3–7 were never written. Packing the later pages onto the next free days — the ordinary scheme's rule, which suits a course whose pages sit on consecutive class days — would move old Week 8 to 2025-10-09, SIX WEEKS EARLIER, while the plan said “moved onto later class days”. In a numbered course a page moves only as far as it must: a page already dated after the page before it stays where it is, and otherwise it takes the first class day after that page. For a section with no gaps the two rules give the same dates (the case above). NOR is a page RENAMED unless the new number lands on its name: old Week 2 becomes Week 3, and Week 8 and Week 9 keep their names and their links — number 3 was free, so the run stops there. (The first version of this case renamed Week 8 → 9 and Week 9 → 10 as well; the #267 implementation review measured that as two published meetings renamed, links rewritten, for nothing.) Found by the #267 plan review; measured against the real planner.

cases.name: making room at a GAP in a numbered course fills the free slot and renames and moves nothing
cases.why: CODING exactly as it is on disk (#267 implementation review, HIGH). A numbered course orders by DATE: the new Week 3 goes after Week 2 — the latest page numbered below it — on the first free class day, 2025-10-02. Week 8 and Week 9 are already later, so nothing is renamed and nothing moves, and the plan lists no move. Measured on the first version: the new page took Week 8's day (2025-11-20) and Week 8 → Week 9 on 11-27, Week 9 → Week 10 on 12-04 — two published meetings renamed and pushed a week later to make room in a slot that was empty.

cases.name: only the run of pages the new number collides with is renamed and moved
cases.why: When the new page DOES land on a name and a day that are taken, the pages it collides with shift — renamed highest first, each onto the first class day after the page before it — and each half stops on its own terms: renaming stops at the first page whose number is already clear (Week 8: the next free number is 6), and moving stops mattering at the first page whose date is already later than the page before it (2025-11-20 is after 2025-10-16). This is the only shape in which a numbered course's plan says pages moved.

cases.name: a numbered page with no date is placed by its number and never given a date
cases.why: An entry with no `date` is a page with no `created`. The old Week 1 becomes Week 2 and STAYS undated: it has no date to collide with, and nothing forces one on it. The fix round's first version sorted undated pages last and dated the old Week 1 2025-11-27 — after Week 8 — so once published the front page, which follows the latest date, would have jumped to it (#267 fix review). An undated page is placed among the dated ones by its NUMBER.

cases.name: when no page has a date, making room dates only the new page
cases.why: Nothing collides, so nothing moves: the first version gave Week 8 the date 2025-09-25 and listed it as moved to a later day (#267 fix review). The new page takes the first class day, there being no dated page below it.

insertion.note: Making room for a class in the middle of a unit. The RENAME ORDER is the part to get right and the part that looks like an implementation detail: it is the difference between a course that survives and one that loses a lesson.

numberedPosition.note: Where “make room” lands in a numbered course (#267), read from the tool's two arguments. The schema still says `unit` and `atDay` and is not changed — routing was measured against it — so “make room at Week 5” may arrive in either, or as a Unit/Day habit's `unit: 5, atDay: 1`. Every reading that names one number is taken; two DIFFERENT numbers, neither of them 1, are refused (null) so the teacher is asked rather than having pages renamed at a guess. Mac: ClassInsertionPlanner.numberedPosition.

cases.why: What a model used to Unit/Day writes for “Week 5”. Reading it as position 1 would make room at the very first meeting and report success.
Two numbers, neither of them 1: no reading is safe, and a wrong one renames pages the teacher's links point at.

positionInSentences.note: Where the room is made, as the two make-room sentences say it — the plan card's “Make room for … at {position} in {code} Section {n}.” and the result's “Made room for … at {position}.” — is the position named the way the COURSE names a page, never “Unit {unit}, Day {day}” typed by hand. Typed by hand is how a Module course was told “at Unit 3, Day 4” and how a club would have been told “at Unit 1, Day 5” (#268, fixed with #267). Each case gives the course's `term` (default “Unit”) and `scheme` (default the ordinary one) and the position, and expects `position`. Mac: ClassInsertionPlan.positionTitle; NumberedCourseTests asserts both sentences.

cases.why: The course's own word — the #268 fault.
One number, and no Day.

cases.name: the copy is the source's own next day, not a page after the last class
cases.why: "Duplicate Unit 1, Day 1 as my next class" means tomorrow's lesson is a copy of that one. Landing the copy after the last class of the course would put it weeks away from the lesson it repeats, and leave the day the teacher meant holding the old page.

cases.name: a later unit re-dated is enough to withhold the undo, even with nothing renamed
cases.why: The case a renames-only test cannot see. Renames happen only WITHIN the unit being changed, so duplicating the last day of a unit renames nothing while re-dating every class of every later unit. An undo keyed on renames alone is offered here and takes back only the new page, leaving the rest of the year moved — a partial undo, which is worse than none. The way back is the backup, and the reply says so.

cases.name: duplicating the last class of the course moves nothing, so it can be taken back
cases.why: Nothing else moves, so taking the copy back is whole rather than partial — and this is the common case, since a teacher duplicating a lesson is usually working at the end of what they have written.

cases.name: a numbered course duplicates as the next number
cases.why: The first case's rule under the one-number scheme (#267): the copy is the source's own next number, and what was there moves up one and onto the next class day.

cases.name: duplicating into a gap in a numbered course renames and moves nothing, so it can be taken back
cases.why: CODING as it is on disk (#267 implementation review, HIGH): “Duplicate Week 2 as my next meeting”. The copy is Week 3, on the first class day after Week 2 — 2025-10-02 — and Week 8 and Week 9 are already later, so neither is renamed or moved and the copy can be taken back. The first version dated the copy 2025-11-20 (Week 8's day) and renamed Week 8 → 9 and Week 9 → 10.

forcedUnpublished.why: The copy starts hidden however the source was. A page made by duplicating a published lesson is a draft of next week's, and putting it in front of students the moment it is made is the one thing duplicating must not do. The per-section publish key has to be checked as well as the plain one: a copied page carrying publishForSection<N>: true beats the publish: false written over it, and the copy would be visible.

undoRule.rule: record undo ONLY when nothing else moved - no renames AND no date moves
undoRule.why: A partial undo that deleted the copy and left every later class renamed and re-dated is worse than no undo at all. When classes shuffled, the way back is the backup taken before any of it, and the reply names it.

duplication.note: Duplicating a lesson as the next class. BOTH suites run all three cases plus forcedUnpublished and undoRule, through the real tool rather than through a re-implementation of the rule, and they ask for the undo the way a teacher does — Windows in ClassPlanningContractTests.Duplication_MatchesContract, the mac in ClassPlanningContractTests.testDuplicatingMatchesTheContract. Proposed FROM Windows 2026-09-18 (#149). The second case — "a later unit re-dated is enough to withhold the undo, even with nothing renamed" — was RED on the mac when its runner was first written, because AssistToolRunner keyed the duplicate's undo on renames.isEmpty alone; mac issue #163 widened it to ClassInsertionPlan.movesAnythingElse, which is the property make-room had used all along. That red run is the handover working rather than damage, and it is recorded here because a case nobody remembers catching anything gets "simplified" out. expectOtherClassesMoving is the number a teacher reads on the plan card before pressing Go: the UNION of renamed and re-dated pages, counted once each (case 1 renames one page and re-dates two, and the answer is 2, not 3). Windows' loop indexes by name and simply does not read it yet — see mac-proposed issue for #163.

cases.why: A section with no numbered class at all starts at Unit 1, Day 1.
The highest UNIT wins, then the highest day within it — a new class belongs to the unit the teacher is currently in, not to whichever unit has the most days.
A numbered course (#267) with no page yet starts at “Week 1”. A runner asserts the NUMBER and builds the title from the course's word; there is no unit.

Russell's CODING club, as it is on disk: weeks 3–7 were never written. The next page is one past the HIGHEST number — never a gap filled — because the number counts meetings and a gap is meetings that had no page.
A page named some other way is passed over, as it is under the ordinary scheme.
A two-number page in a numbered course is not a class page (pageNaming), so it cannot push the count along.

CODING as it is on disk, with its DATES (#267 implementation review, HIGH). A numbered course orders by date, so the next page is dated one class day after the LATEST page — Week 9's 2025-11-27 — not by position (four pages → the fifth date, 2025-10-16, which the first version wrote: five weeks BEFORE Week 8, where the front page, which follows the latest date, never showed it). A runner builds the plan through the real planner with this timetable remembered and asserts the title AND the date. A case with `existingClasses` has no `existing`: it is the dated form.

nextClass.note: What 'add the next class' would be called: the highest unit these pages name, and one past the highest day inside it. In a numbered course (#267), one past the highest number — and a case that carries `timetable` and `expectDate` also pins its DATE: one class day after the latest dated page, because a numbered course orders by date and may have gaps.

note: Naming, numbering and making room for classes. All of it is pure rules over page titles and dates, so all of it is portable. The insertion cases are the highest-stakes data in these contracts: they rename files a teacher's lessons live in.

numberedClassOrder.note: Numbered pages sort by unit, then by day — not by date and not by filename.
numberedClassOrder.why: Day 10 after Day 2, so this cannot be a string sort. And 'Field Trip' is dropped from the list rather than sorted to one end.

numberedScheme.why: The same rule under the one-number scheme (#267): by number, never as strings (Week 10 after Week 2), with the unnumbered page dropped.

cases.title: Unit 2 Day 4
cases.why: The comma is part of the form. Accepting near-misses means guessing at what a teacher meant by a name, and the cost of guessing wrong is a renamed lesson.

cases.title: Module 2, Day 3
cases.why: A course that says Module. Its pages are named this way as the course is made — see file-formats.json, `unit_word`.

cases.title: Unit 2, Day 3
cases.why: The load-bearing case, and the one that fails silently if it is got wrong. In a Module course a page called "Unit 2, Day 3" is NOT a class page. Reading it as one would put two numbering schemes in one section, and reading it as one only sometimes is worse still.

cases.title: thread 1, day 1
cases.why: Case-insensitive, exactly as the default word already is.

cases.title: Week 3
cases.why: A club (#267): class_page_scheme "numbered" names a page with ONE number. It is read as unit 1, day 3 — every planner then counts one number with no rewrite — but a runner must assert the NUMBER, never a unit.

cases.title: week 12
cases.why: Case-insensitive, as the other scheme is.

cases.title: Week 3, Day 1
cases.why: Nothing may follow the number. A two-number page in a numbered course is not a class page — reading it as one would put two schemes in one section.

cases.title: Unit 1, Day 1
cases.why: The skeleton's first page is not a club's class page; this is why a numbered course is poured no skeleton.

cases.title: Weekly Notes
cases.why: The word must be followed by whitespace and a number.

cases.title: Week 3
cases.why: The same title under the ORDINARY scheme is not a class page. This is the state of a course whose pages are “Week N” but whose configuration says nothing about a scheme (Russell's CODING club): it stays exactly as it was, and nothing converts it.

pageNaming.note: Which class-page titles carry numbers. A page named some other way — 'Field Trip', 'Exam Review' — is NOT guessed at: it is passed over everywhere classes are renumbered, and keeps its own date. The plan says how many were skipped so nobody is surprised. A case with no `term` uses the default word, “Unit” — which is what a course says when `unit_word` is absent from its configuration, and what every course made before 2026-09-01 says. A case with `"scheme": "numbered"` is read under that course's ONE-number scheme (file-formats.json, `class_page_scheme`; #267) and carries `expectNumber` instead of a unit and a day; a case with no `scheme` is the ordinary one, which is what an absent key means.

cases.why: Numbers start at 1 under the one-number scheme too.

A numbered course (#267) has one run of pages and no units, so “start a new unit” has nothing to act on. Refused BEFORE the class dates are asked for, so nobody is asked for their dates on the way to being told no.
“Add three more days to Unit 1” is the same request in another shape, and gets the same answer.

refusals.note: Named by case, not by message: which refusal it is must match on both platforms, while the sentence a teacher reads is the product's wording.

wholeUnit.note: Which request names a WHOLE unit — “publish Unit 4”, “hide Module 4” — rather than one page. A whole unit is published or hidden one class page at a time; a title that is not a unit goes to the ordinary page path, which acts on the one page named. Each case reads `title` in a course whose word is `term` (default “Unit”) under `scheme` (default the ordinary one) and expects the unit NUMBER, or null for “not a whole unit”. Mac: AssistPublishPlanner.unitNamed.

cases.title: unit 4.
cases.why: Case and a trailing full stop are forgiven: the model echoes what a teacher typed.

cases.title: Module 4
cases.why: The course's own word names a unit — reading only “unit” meant a Module course found nothing and was told no page is called that.

cases.title: Unit 4
cases.why: “unit” is accepted beside the course's word: the NUMBER is the answer either way, so accepting both cannot be ambiguous.

cases.title: Unit 4, Day 3
cases.why: A day was named, so this is one page.

cases.title: Week 1
cases.why: The CRITICAL case of #267. A numbered course's pages are “Week 1”, “Week 2”, and an app that holds them as one unit (the mac holds them as unit 1) would read “publish Week 1” — the most ordinary request a club has — as the whole of unit 1 and publish EVERY meeting at once, with a card that did not say so. A numbered course has no units: every title goes to the page path. Measured on the mac before the fix: the real parser read “Week 1” as unit 1, and publishing it in a four-page numbered section published four pages.

cases.title: Week 3
cases.why: The other half of the same fault: read as “unit 3” it found no unit and was REFUSED, instead of publishing the page.

cases.title: Unit 1
cases.why: “unit” is not a numbered course's word either, so “publish unit 1” typed in a club reaches the page path and is told no page is called that — never the whole course.

classFolder.note: Which folder holds a section's class pages, and whether a given page is one of them. ONE rule, because there were several and they disagreed — a teacher whose folder was not called 'All Classes' got a different answer from the mac app, the Windows app and the build, and the build's answer silently changed the Curriculum Coverage map from 'pages the course teaches' to 'every published page'. A wrong map that reports success is the failure this rule exists to close.

naming.rule: WHERE A NEW CLASS PAGE IS WRITTEN. Read from the course's own configured per_section_folders, never guessed from what is on disk: the first entry whose name contains 'class' (case-insensitive), else the first entry, else the literal 'All Classes'. Substring matching is safe HERE because the list is a short curated one the teacher chose; it is NOT safe against arbitrary paths, which is what isClassPage below is careful about.

cases.name: the ordinary case
a teacher's own name for it
cases.why: Contains 'class', so it wins over the earlier entry. This is the case that was broken: the build matched only the exact strings 'all classes' and 'classes', so this course's lessons were invisible to it while both apps found them.

cases.name: case-insensitive
nothing mentions classes
cases.why: The first entry, so a course still has somewhere to put a class page rather than failing.

cases.name: no per-section folders at all
cases.why: The last-resort literal. A section with nothing configured still gets a predictable answer instead of an empty path.

cases.name: a recorded folder with no 'class' in its name
cases.why: The case the key exists for. A teacher whose units are Threads and whose classes are Days calls the folder 'All Days'; the guess returns it here only by accident of it being first, and returns 'Tasks' the moment the list is ordered the other way.

cases.name: a recorded folder that is not first
cases.why: Proves the key beats position. Without it this course's class pages would be written into Tasks.

cases.name: the record beats the guess
cases.why: A folder mentioning 'class' is present and is NOT the class folder. The teacher said which one; the guess does not get a vote.

cases.name: a record naming a folder that is no longer there
cases.why: A stale key must not win. Falling back to the guess keeps a course working after somebody removes the recorded folder in Obsidian; honouring the stale name would point the next-class button at a folder that is not there.

cases.name: the record's spelling loses to the list's
cases.why: Matched case-insensitively, but the LIST's spelling is returned: everything downstream builds file paths out of this answer, and on a case-sensitive volume the key's spelling would not be there.

cases.name: a club's folder, recorded, below another folder
cases.why: A club's class pages live in “All Meetings”, which does not say 'class'. The guess alone answers “Resources” here (measured, #267), so the recorded name is the only thing that finds the meetings — and the course setup must pass it in rather than re-guess, or the next re-run writes the wrong folder back.

isClassPage.rule: A page is a class page when it is NOT an index.md and one of its FOLDER segments — never its file name — equals ANY of the membership names above, case-insensitively. Segments are taken RELATIVE to the content root (or the section folder); the path above it is the teacher's own filing and means nothing here. Either path separator is understood.
isClassPage.whyFolderSegmentsOnly: Defence in depth, not a bug that was observed. Under segment EQUALITY a file name can never collide with a folder name (a page is 'x.md' and a folder is 'x'), so excluding the file name changes no answer today. It is kept so that a future change to prefix or substring matching cannot silently start counting a page because of what it is CALLED — 'How This Class Works.md' ships in about twenty payloads, and ADA1O ships a curriculum expectation page called 'B3. Connections Beyond the Classroom.md'. An earlier draft of this contract claimed those pages HAD been miscounted; that was wrong — the previous build rule was equality too — and the claim is corrected here rather than left to be believed.
isClassPage.whyRelativeToTheContentRoot: Every implementation had this wrong somewhere. build_site.py walked `page.parts` of an ABSOLUTE path (content_root.rglob yields absolute paths), Windows tested the whole directory STRING, and the mac's AssistSectionGraph returns the FULL ABSOLUTE PATH whenever workspaceURL is nil — which SectionIndexPointer.repointIndex passes. So a teacher whose working folder was 'C:\\Users\\x\\Classroom' or '~/Documents/All Classes' made every page in every course a class page. Where a teacher keeps their files is not a fact about their lessons.

cases.name: the ordinary case
nested inside the class folder
cases.why: Any folder segment, at any depth — a teacher who files lessons by unit has not stopped teaching them.

cases.name: case-insensitive
a folder index is never a class page
cases.why: A folder index carries the same date as the first class, and treating it as a lesson would let a reshuffle move the way in to the folder.

cases.name: the file name is ignored
cases.why: Ships in about twenty payloads. The old build rule counted it.

cases.name: a curriculum page that mentions a classroom
cases.why: Ships in ADA1O. An expectation page is not a lesson.

cases.name: a folder that merely contains the word
cases.why: The segment must EQUAL the class folder's name. A classics course's reference folder is not where its lessons live.

cases.name: a teacher's own class folder
the old hardcoded name, when it is not this course's
cases.why: The rule follows the COURSE's configured folder, not a name that used to be hardcoded.

cases.name: a Windows path separator
cases.why: The same relative path arrives with either separator depending on the platform that produced it, and one implementation understanding only '/' is a divergence hiding inside a shared rule.

cases.name: the second of two class folders
cases.why: Membership is every configured folder that mentions classes, not only the one a new page would be written to.

cases.name: a page in the OTHER class folder

membership.rule: WHICH FOLDERS COUNT AS HOLDING CLASS PAGES — every configured per_section_folder whose name contains 'class' (case-insensitive); if none does, just the single name `naming` chose.
membership.why: Naming and membership are the same question only when a course has ONE such folder. A course configured ["Class Resources", "All Classes"] would otherwise resolve to 'Class Resources' for both, match zero pages, and drop the coverage map back to 'every published page' — reintroducing the exact silent failure this rule was written to close. Writing goes to one folder; counting looks at all of them.

cases.name: the ordinary case
a class folder beside one that mentions no classes
cases.why: Only the folder that mentions classes counts. Handouts are course material, not days of teaching, and counting them puts them in the dated class lists, in 'publish every class from the 15th', and in the list of classes a scheduled deploy says students cannot see yet. Windows walked every per_section_folder in two places and did exactly that until 2026-09-19 (issue #115); the mac and build_site.py never did.

cases.name: two folders that both mention classes
cases.why: Both count. Only the first is where a NEW page is written.

cases.name: nothing mentions classes
cases.why: Falls back to whatever `naming` chose, so a course still has one answer.

cases.name: no per-section folders at all
a recorded folder counts, and so does a class-mentioning one
cases.why: The recorded folder first, then the guess's answers. Dropping the class-mentioning folder would SHRINK what the course is seen to teach, which is the direction that produces the wrong map; adding the recorded one can only widen it. A course that had 'Class Resources' counting yesterday must not lose it by recording a class folder today.

cases.name: a recorded folder that also mentions classes is counted once

renamingTheUnitWord.note: Renaming a course's word for a unit after the course is in use (issue #100, 2026-09-10). Pure rules over page titles: which pages are renamed, what refuses the whole rename, and how links follow. The sentences are in shared-rules.json → specialNames.renameUnitWord. Reference implementation: UnitWordRenamer (mac). Each case builds a course with the given sections and pages, plans a rename from `from` to `to`, and compares. `expectRefused` true means the plan lists NO renames and at least one problem; `expectRenames` is every page that would move, as {section, from, to}; anything not listed is left alone.
renamingTheUnitWord.why: Chosen at course creation and, until this, nowhere else — because renaming an existing course's word means rewriting every class page's name, its frontmatter title and every wikilink pointing at it, and a half-finished pass leaves a broken site. What made it safe was not scale (a ready-made course holds 84–87 class pages, 42 for CHV2O and GLC2O) but an undo: the operation is its own inverse (rename it back), a backup of the whole course is saved first, and a rename that stops part way is recognised and finished by running it again. REJECTED: a display-only rename (titles say Thread while files stay Unit — Obsidian is the teacher's editor and they would see the old word every time); rewriting prose ('by the end of Unit 3' is the teacher's own writing after creation); skipping a page that already sits where a renamed page would go (two numbering schemes in one section); skipping a page that cannot be read (the configuration would then name a word half the pages do not use).

howAPageIsRenamed.rule: The title inside the frontmatter is set to the new name IN PLACE, then the file is MOVED. Never copied and deleted.
howAPageIsRenamed.why: A move is atomic on one volume, so there is never a moment with two copies or none — an interruption leaves a page under its old name whose title says the new one, which is harmless because every reader goes by the file name, and a second run finishes it. Copy-then-delete (the insertion planner's shape) interrupted between the two leaves both files, and the plan's own collision rule would then refuse the very re-run meant to finish it. A page with no title line is moved without one: Quartz falls back to the file name. Whether a destination that 'exists' is the SOURCE — a change of capitalisation on a case-insensitive volume — is asked of the filesystem's file identity, never of the spelling, so a case-sensitive volume still sees a genuine clash.

order: read every planned page (an unreadable one refuses everything)
write the record that a rename is under way
rewrite links across every page of the course, shared folders included
renamingTheUnitWord.orderWhy: Disk first, configuration last: if a move fails nothing has been written and the course is as it was. Links after moves so a link can never point at a name that is not there yet. The backup before the record, so a record can never exist without a way back.

cases.name: every numbered page in every section moves; anything else stays
a page named with a different word is not a class page and is left alone
cases.why: Only the course's CURRENT word names a class page. 'Unit 1, Day 1' in a Module course is somebody's own page, whatever it looks like.

cases.name: the match is case-insensitive, as the parser already is
a page already sitting where a renamed page would go refuses the whole rename
cases.why: Not one page skipped — the whole rename refused. Two numbering schemes in one section is worse than no rename.

cases.name: a course with no class pages yet is allowed: only the settings would change
cases.why: A brand-new course, or one whose class pages are all named some other way. The word still decides what the next class is called, so changing it is meaningful.

cases.name: finishing an interrupted rename: pages already moved are not matched, and links to their old names are still followed
cases.why: A rename that stopped after the first page. Running it again must finish: the moved page is under the new word and is not planned again, but a link written as [[Unit 1, Day 1]] still needs to follow it, so the link map covers both.

cases.name: finishing an interrupted change of capitalisation: a page already spelled the new way is not moved onto itself
cases.why: The parser is case-insensitive, so on a re-run the page already moved matches the OLD word too. Its new title equals its title: it is left where it is rather than moved onto itself — which the mac's filesystem tolerates and others may not — and stays in the link map so [[Unit 1, Day 1]] is still repointed. Found by the implementation review, 2026-09-10.

linkCases.note: How links follow renamed pages. Each case rewrites `text` with the link map a rename from `from` to `to` builds over `pageTitles`, and expects `expect`. The rewriter is the one the insertion planner already uses (WikiLinkRewriter on the mac): it changes only the page name between the brackets and stops at #, | and ].

cases.name: a plain link, an alias, a heading and a transclusion all follow; the alias is the teacher's own words

cases.expect: See [[Module 2, Day 3]] and [[Module 2, Day 3|the lesson on loops]], [[Module 2, Day 3#Agenda]], ![[Module 2, Day 3]].

cases.name: prose that mentions a unit by number is not touched
cases.text: By the end of Unit 3 you will link to [[Unit 3, Day 1]] and read Unit 3 of the textbook.
cases.expect: By the end of Unit 3 you will link to [[Module 3, Day 1]] and read Unit 3 of the textbook.

cases.name: a link to a page that is not a class page is not touched even when it starts with the word

sectionIndexPointer.note: Which line of a section's front page (`sectionN/index.md`) is repointed when a newer class page becomes visible (#267). The front page opens by transcluding ONE class page — the newest one students can see — under a heading the course chose when it was created: “# Most Recent Class” for a course, “# Most Recent Meeting” for a club (`course_config.json` → `front_page_heading`), and whatever the teacher typed in a course made by hand (CODING's is “## Most Recent Meeting”, an h2). The embed is FOUND BY WHICH PAGE IT NAMES — the first line that transcludes one of the section's class pages — never by the heading. The heading is written once, at creation, and is never read or rewritten by repointing: that is why a hand-worded front page keeps working, and why an existing course keeps its heading. `indexBody` is the page BELOW its frontmatter; the cases carry no dates, so the frontmatter's `created:` (which follows the class it points at) is out of scope here — the date rule is the mac's own test. `expectBody: null` means the page is left exactly as it is. Which page is newest (date, then the course's own numbering) is also out of scope: `pointAt` names it.
sectionIndexPointer.found: The first line, anywhere in the page, whose trimmed text is `![[…]]` and whose target — before any `|` display name or `#` heading, and after any folder path — is one of the section's class-page titles (case-insensitive). That one line becomes `![[<pointAt>]]`; every other byte is left alone.
sectionIndexPointer.neverFoundBy: The heading text. A front page headed anything, at any level, or with no heading at all, is repointed the same way; a transclusion of a page that is NOT a class page (Help Sessions, Key Links) is never replaced, whatever heading it sits under.

whenNoClassIsTransclusion.mac: Left as it is. The mac never inserts an embed: it cannot know where on a teacher's page one belongs, and a club's front page is created WITH its first embed (`setup_course.py` → the club start), so a page with none is one the teacher emptied on purpose.
whenNoClassIsTransclusion.windows: Inserts `![[<pointAt>]]` on the line directly after the course's front-page heading — the line whose trimmed text is `#`s, a space and `front_page_heading` (absent → “Most Recent Class”), at any level, case-insensitive — and leaves the page alone when there is no such heading. This is Windows' shipped behaviour for “# Most Recent Class” (`SectionIndex.WithMostRecent`), kept, and widened to the course's own heading.
whenNoClassIsTransclusion.why: Stated rather than settled, on purpose: the two apps already differ here and neither behaviour has cost a teacher anything, so the contract pins BOTH and says which is which (`expectBodyOnWindows`), rather than breaking one app's shipped behaviour to make them match. A case whose `expectBodyOnWindows` is present is the ONLY place the two may differ; everywhere else `expectBody` binds both.

cases.name: CODING's hand-made front page: an h2 in the teacher's own words, no blank line, no final newline
cases.why: The fixture this issue came from. Its heading is neither the course default nor at h1, and it carries no `front_page_heading` key — found by the page it names, it repoints; found by heading, it would never move.

cases.name: a club's front page as it is created
a transclusion of a page that is not a class is never replaced, even directly under the heading
cases.expectBodyOnWindows:
# Most Recent Class
![[Unit 1, Day 1]]

![[Help Sessions]]

![[Key Links]]
cases.why: The “far worse bug” `SectionIndexPointer`'s own comment names: repointing Help Sessions at a lesson removes it from the page every student lands on. Neither app may replace it. The mac leaves the page alone; Windows inserts the class embed above it (`whenNoClassIsTransclusion`).

cases.name: a front page with no heading at all
cases.why: A course set up from scratch writes a front page with frontmatter only; a teacher who adds a class embed to it without a heading gets it repointed like any other.

cases.name: an embed with a folder path and a display name
cases.why: The target is what comes before `|` or `#`, after the last `/`. The replacement is the bare title: the display name and path are not carried over.
